source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 24. Exercises reused from the lesson.

title.en: Stealing — and owning up to mistakes

topic: Never take what isn't yours; admit and correct mistakes

learn.en: Stealing is taking someone's things secretly without permission, not meaning to give them back. It is an evil act.
learn.title: What is stealing?

learn.en: Your classmates' pens, pencils, rubbers and crayons belong to them. Taking them without asking — or by force — is stealing.
learn.title: Not mine

learn.en: Islam's teaching about stealing is very strict (Qur'an 5:38). Never start taking even small things, or it can grow into a bad habit.
learn.title: Very serious

learn.en: We all make mistakes. What is done can't be undone — so tell the truth, admit it, fix it, learn from it and ask Allah's forgiveness.
learn.title: Owning up

learn.en: Hiding a mistake with a lie is a second mistake. Owning up gives us courage to obey Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.
learn.title: Be brave

quiz.en: You find a pencil on the classroom floor. You…
opts: give it to the teacher or ask whose it is

quiz.en: You broke something by mistake. The best thing is to…
opts: tell the truth and fix it

quiz.en: True or false? Taking a classmate's crayon without asking is stealing.
True or false? Small things don't matter, so it's OK to take them.

think.q: Think of a time you made a mistake. Did you own up? How did it feel afterwards?
think.a: Owning up feels scary at first, but then light and brave — and Allah loves it.

parents.summary: Stealing is taking without permission — serious in Islam; when we err we admit it, fix it, and say astaghfiru-llāh.
parents.tip: Praise honesty more than the mistake — make owning up safe at home.
